auditor_runtime: Codex desktop, isolated in-app Chromium browser, black-box first-user pass followed by source-assisted diagnosis

findings.title: Node inspection and vector movement are pointer-only
findings.resolution_evidence: The Inspect panel now exposes a labelled node selector and labelled X/Y coordinate fields with a Move node action. Browser retest selected node 0 and moved it to [400, 200] without canvas interaction; the update trace was generated.
findings.preconditions: A populated graph is visible and Inspect mode is selected.
steps_to_reproduce: Use keyboard-only navigation to select Inspect.
Attempt to select a graph node or change its vector without clicking or dragging the SVG.
findings.expected: A keyboard and non-drag single-pointer alternative should allow selecting a node and changing its position.
findings.observed: The SVG is exposed as one image named 'HNSW graph'; its nodes are not focusable controls. The UI instructs users to drag a node, and no coordinate fields, node list, or move controls are available.
evidence: Keyboard search was reachable, but node selection could only be completed by a coordinate click and movement only by dragging.
src/components/GraphCanvas.tsx:301-315 binds pointer events to an SVG with role=img and no keyboard interaction.
findings.user_impact: Keyboard-only users and users who cannot perform precise dragging cannot complete the inspect/update learning flow.
findings.fix_direction: Add a keyboard-operable node list or make nodes individually focusable, and provide coordinate inputs or directional move buttons as a drag alternative.
findings.retest: From a fresh Playground session, select and move a node, then verify its update trace, using keyboard only and without drag.

findings.title: Small muted text does not meet normal-text contrast
findings.resolution_evidence: The muted text token is now #70726b in light mode and #858a80 in dark mode. Browser-computed contrast measured 4.70:1 on #fbfbf9 and 5.04:1 on #171816.
findings.location: Landing page and repeated muted labels/hints across the product
findings.preconditions: Light/system theme rendering a light color scheme.
steps_to_reproduce: Open the landing page in the light theme.
Inspect the eyebrow and footnote text colors against the page background.
findings.expected: Normal text below large-text thresholds should reach at least 4.5:1 contrast.
findings.observed: The 10-10.5px muted text uses #888a82 on #fbfbf9, producing approximately 3.38:1 contrast.
evidence: Computed styles: rgb(136, 138, 130) on rgb(251, 251, 249), 10-10.5px, weight 400-600.
src/styles.css:12 defines --text-3 as #888a82 and applies it throughout small labels and hints.
findings.user_impact: Low-vision users and users on lower-quality or glare-affected displays may miss labels, hints, legends, and status metadata.
findings.fix_direction: Darken --text-3 for text use, or split the token so decorative strokes can remain light while small text reaches 4.5:1.
findings.retest: All normal-size uses of the muted text token measure at least 4.5:1 in each theme.

findings.title: Learning content refers to old tab names
findings.resolution_evidence: All user-facing obsolete tab names were updated to Tune, Trace, and Results. A rendered-copy regression assertion and repository search cover the stale forms.
findings.location: Learn chapters and Lab explanatory copy
findings.preconditions: The user is following a tutorial or reading a Lab result.
steps_to_reproduce: Read the local-minimum, layers, pruning, or production chapters.
Compare the named destination tabs with the Playground tab bar.
findings.expected: Instructions should use the visible tab names: Tune, Trace, and Results.
findings.observed: Multiple passages say Params, Code, or Metrics even though the current tabs are Tune, Trace, and Results. Lab output also tells the user to use the Params tab.
evidence: Visible Playground tabs: Build, Tune, Trace, Inspect, Results, Lab.
src/lessons/lessons.ts:157,258,374,770 and src/components/panels/LabPanel.tsx:91 use stale names.
findings.user_impact: A learner following exact instructions hesitates or searches for tabs that do not exist, weakening trust in otherwise strong educational content.
findings.fix_direction: Replace stale labels with the current user-facing tab names and add a copy-level regression test for known obsolete labels.
findings.retest: A repository-wide and rendered-page check finds no user-facing references to Params, Code, or Metrics as Playground tab names.

findings.title: Refreshing silently discards the entire experiment
findings.resolution_evidence: Versioned sessionStorage persistence now restores settings, graph Maps, selection, active panel, and trace data while safely pausing playback. Browser retest restored selected node 0 at X=400 after reload; serialization round-trip tests cover graph and trace Maps.
findings.preconditions: The user has changed settings, inserted or moved a vector, or generated a trace.
steps_to_reproduce: Open Playground and change M from 5 to 2.
Insert a vector so the count changes from 48 to 49, or move a node.
findings.expected: Either the in-progress experiment should be restored, or the UI should clearly state that the playground is temporary before a refresh causes loss.
findings.observed: The graph, settings, selected node, trace, and vector count all return to defaults without warning. Theme preference persists, which makes the lack of experiment persistence less obvious.
evidence: Observed vector count 49 and completed insert trace before refresh; count returned to 48 and M returned to 5 after refresh.
src/state/StoreProvider.tsx:5 initializes reducer state on every load and contains no state restoration path.
findings.user_impact: Users can lose a multi-step learning setup or comparison and must reconstruct it manually.
findings.fix_direction: Persist serializable experiment state per session, or add explicit save/share/reset controls and a clear ephemeral-state warning.
findings.retest: After changing settings and graph state, refresh restores the experiment exactly or presents an explicit, user-approved reset path.

findings.title: The sub-900px gate blocks the landing page and text-only guide, not only the graph
findings.resolution_evidence: The sub-900px gate is scoped to route-playground. Landing and Learn receive single-column mobile reflow rules, while the Playground gate links directly to the mobile-friendly guide. The route/render contract and production CSS were verified; the browser runtime did not permit viewport emulation for a second visual capture.
steps_to_reproduce: Open the site at a 390x844 viewport.
Attempt to access the landing page or Learn route.
findings.expected: The graph workbench may require desktop width, but the product introduction and text-first Learn content should remain available when they can reflow safely.
findings.observed: A 'The graph needs more room' gate replaces every route and offers no link to read the guide or continue with a limited experience.
evidence: src/styles.css:328-331 hides every app child except the gate below 900px.
findings.user_impact: Mobile and narrow-window visitors cannot evaluate the product, read its tutorial, or bookmark learning material until they switch devices.
findings.fix_direction: Apply the width gate only to the Playground workbench; let landing and Learn routes reflow, with a clear desktop CTA for interactive graph exercises.
findings.retest: At 390px, landing and Learn are readable and navigable; Playground shows a focused desktop-width limitation without hiding the rest of the site.
